title: Mastering diverse control tasks through world models (DreamerV3)
description: Nature article (arXiv title 'Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models') presenting DreamerV3, a model-based reinforcement-learning algorithm that learns a world model of the environment and improves its behaviour by imagining future scenarios. The learning algorithm comprises world model learning, critic learning, actor learning and 'robust predictions' techniques, run with one fixed configuration across Atari (57 games), ProcGen (16), DMLab (30), Atari100k (26), the Proprio Control and Visual Control suites (20 tasks each), BSuite (23 environments) and Minecraft, where it is reported as the first algorithm to collect diamonds from scratch without human data or curricula. The evaluation also covers ablations and scaling properties.
codeLicence: github.com/danijar/dreamerv3: MIT License (GitHub licence API spdx MIT; LICENSE 'Copyright (c) 2024 Danijar Hafner'). A JAX implementation; its README states it is based on the DreamerV2 codebase and is unrelated to Google or DeepMind.

arXiv version: CC BY 4.0 (abstract-page licence link).

Host terms: nature.com's Website Terms prohibit non-browser access and PMC prohibits automated article downloads outside its OA services, so the Nature version is cited, not imported; arXiv v2 may be imported from arxiv.org.
The code repository is MIT-licensed; the paper's data availability statement says the algorithm generates its own experience data by interacting with simulated environments.

Corniversity decision (2026-10-31): the CC BY arXiv preprint is the working copy, because it may be imported for private study; the Nature article is the version of record, read in the browser and cited for the published results. The two texts were not compared line by line.
